anomalies.obs: On the Power sheet, the +12V up-arrow feeds a vertical wire that joins BOTH pin 1 and pin 2 of each 4-pin fan header (J7 and J8), with junction dots at both rows; pin 3 carries FAN_0_TACH/FAN_1_TACH and pin 4 is a no-connect. No pin of either header is tied to GND.
anomalies.exp: A 4-pin fan header's pin 1 is the fan ground; the specification lists only 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)' on the +12V net, so pin 1 must be GND (the return path for the fan motor and the reference for the open-collector tach signal).

evidence.quote: Power sheet (power.kicad_sch): J7/J8 Conn_01x04 — +12V arrow wire with green junction dots at pin 1 and pin 2; pin 3 -> FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH; pin 4 -> NC; no GND symbol on the header.
Section 3 Inputs: '+12V net. Also on this net: ... the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2).'

anomalies.impact: The fan ground pin is driven at +12V instead of 0V, so a connected fan has no supply return (motor sees ~0V across it) and will not spin; the tach open-collector has no ground reference, so FAN_x_TACH reads are invalid and fan-stall detection fails. It also shorts the fan's GND wire to +12V, risking damage to the fan or the 12V rail.
